title: First Game feedback preview 1
author: vispar9999
selftext:
I’m developing my first game, currently called Maze Escape. It’s a 2D cave/maze game built with Python, and I currently have 10 playable levels.

For development, I’ve been using a combination of Python, Aseprite, and generative AI. I use Aseprite for pixel-art work while AI helps me experiment with assets, ideas, and parts of the development process.

I’m still learning and improving the game, so I’d appreciate feedback.

What should I improve most: level design, visuals, difficulty, enemies, or gameplay?

Game: [https://visper99.itch.io/maze-escape](https://visper99.itch.io/maze-escape)

comments.author: broker415
comments.body: Would be helpful to add screenshots or gameplay video, most people will give feedback but won’t play a game that is just a blue link and a description

comments.author: thedev13
comments.body: Are you personally comfortable with Py? Because afaik it's not really used for gamedev

replies.author: vispar9999
replies.body: I’m new to game development, As for now i m a bit comfortable with Python. I know bigger studios use engines like Unreal or Godot wih C++. Since its my first game tbh.

replies.author: vispar9999
replies.body: As an update, I’ll be fixing and improving a lot of things, including adding a soundtrack. There’s currently a bug where pressing **ESC** during the intro/menu can close the entire game. For now, please avoid pressing **ESC in the game menu**. I’ll fix this and other issues in an upcoming update.
